choices.C: Neural networks can often accomplish tasks that biological brains do, but they are typically programmed with rules to model multiple types of brain cells simultaneously.

passage: Born in Chile in 1917, artist and ethnomusicologist Violeta Parra was a pioneer in the nueva canción chilena (Chilean New Song) movement that emerged in the late 1950s and then spread throughout Latin America, Portugal, and Spain as nueva canción . Parra traveled all over Chile compiling extensive records of authentic folk music as well as recipes, proverbs, and other facets of cultural history. These records formed the foundation for the early movement’s revival of traditional Chilean folk forms in new songs that represented modern realities of the working class and strongly advocated for social change. As the movement spread beyond Chile, the breadth of musical traditions incorporated into its foundation also expanded.
prompt: Which detail about songs associated with nueva canción , if true, would best illustrate the underlined claim?

choices.A: Many feature political commentary addressing contemporary issues that stemmed from shared experiences of European colonization in Latin American countries.
choices.B: Many demonstrate the stylistic influence of corrido , a genre of narrative songs from Mexico that had come to be characterized by political themes in the early 1800s.
choices.C: Many were written with parts meant to be played on the quena , a traditional flute used across Andean countries, including Chile.
choices.D: Many were produced by Argentinian artists in the late 1950s, with others by artists in additional Latin American countries first emerging soon after.

rationale: Choice B is the best answer because it presents a detail that, if true, would most effectively illustrate the underlined claim that as nueva canción spread beyond Chile, the breadth of musical traditions incorporated into its foundation also expanded. The text explains that the movement was initially founded on traditional Chilean folk forms compiled by Parra, so if many nueva canción songs demonstrate the stylistic influence of corrido —a Mexican narrative song genre—that would show that a musical tradition originating outside Chile became part of the movement’s foundation, directly illustrating the text’s claim about how the breadth of nueva canción expanded. Choice A is incorrect because the finding addresses lyrical content—political commentary on issues stemming from European colonization—rather than musical traditions. Even if nueva canción songs across different countries share political themes, that doesn’t indicate that new musical forms or styles were incorporated into the movement’s foundation. Thematic content is distinct from the musical traditions that songs draw on stylistically. Choice C is incorrect because the quena is described as a “traditional flute used across Andean countries, including Chile,” meaning it’s part of the Chilean folk tradition that underpinned nueva canción at its origin. Use of the quena therefore wouldn’t illustrate the incorporation of musical traditions beyond those that founded the early movement in Chile. Choice D is incorrect because the finding establishes only that artists in additional Latin American countries produced nueva canción songs, not that those artists incorporated musical traditions from their own countries into the movement. Artists in other countries could still have been drawing on the same Chilean folk forms that originally founded the movement, so geographic spread alone doesn’t illustrate an expansion of musical traditions.

passage: Having demonstrated that the power conversion efficiency of new perovskite photovoltaic cells is nearly indistinguishable from that of cells recycled multiple times, Xun Xiao and colleagues evaluated the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE)—a measure of cost per produced electricity unit that incorporates materials acquisition costs as well as operating costs—for power plants utilizing each type of cell. With a modeled 15-year cell lifetime, the LCOE of plants using new cells was 4.99 cents per kilowatt-hour, whereas that of plants using cells recycled three times was 4.05 cents per kilowatt-hour. Moreover, the LCOE differential grew from 18.8% to 31.3% when the modeled cell lifetime was reduced by two-thirds.
prompt: Based on the text, which choice, if true, most coherently and directly accounts for the observation presented in the underlined sentence?

choices.A: Cells can be recycled multiple times without a significant decrease in power conversion efficiency, and thus recycling cells more frequently does not change the LCOE for plants using recycled cells.
choices.B: Although potentially less expensive than producing new cells, recycling cells does incur costs, and thus reducing cell lifetimes entails greater cumulative costs.
choices.C: Securing new cell materials is more expensive than recycling cell materials, and thus more frequent cell replacement entails greater disparity in cumulative costs.
choices.D: As the modeled cell lifetime decreases, plant operating costs increase, and thus the LCOE for plants using new cells diverges from that of plants using recycled cells.

rationale: Choice C is the best answer because it presents information that, if true, would coherently and directly account for the researchers’ observation about the LCOE differential between plants using new cells and plants using recycled cells. The text explains that the researchers found that the LCOE—a cost-per-unit electricity measure that includes the cost of acquiring the materials—is higher for plants using new cells than for plants using cells recycled three times, with the gap between them growing from 18.8% to 31.3% when the researchers reduced the modeled cell lifetime by two-thirds (that is, from 15 years to 5 years). If obtaining new cell materials were more expensive than recycling preexisting cell materials, then plants using new cells would incur greater materials costs than plants using recycled cells when cells need to be replaced, and the greater frequency of cell replacement entailed by a shorter cell lifetime would force plants using new cells to incur that greater cost more often—widening the gap between those plants and plants using recycled cells. Choice A is incorrect because the information that efficiencies are similar between new and recycled cells (which the text already establishes) and that frequency of recycling doesn’t affect the LCOE for plants using recycled cells wouldn’t address the effect of shorter cell lifetimes on the LCOE of plants using new cells. Information about that effect would be needed to account for the observation that the gap between the LCOEs for the two types of plants widens when cell lifetimes are shortened. Choice B is incorrect. Although the choice does point to the possibility of a scenario that could explain the growth in the LCOE differential (“potentially less expensive than producing new cells”), it presents that information as a concession (“although”) to its central assertion, which is that the cumulative costs would increase if cells had to be replaced more frequently than on the original 15-year timeline. This choice doesn’t indicate whether the increased cumulative costs in question are those of recycled-cell plants or both types of plants; either way, an increase in cumulative costs isn’t a coherent or direct explanation for why the difference in costs between new-cell plants and recycled-cell plants increases when the cell lifetime is reduced by two-thirds. A coherent and direct explanation for growth in the cost difference between the two types of plants must focus on a disparate effect on the plants’ costs; choice B, however, presents information that could be but is not necessarily relevant to a disparate effect and then doesn’t draw the relevant conclusion from it, instead drawing a conclusion about cumulative costs that doesn’t entail a growing differential. rationale: Choice A is the best answer. The student concluded that country-specific factors influence changes to median age of first marriage. The student concluded that country-specific factors influence changes to median age of first marriage. The students’ conclusion is about changes that occurred during the 20th century. This choice provides broad information about the century as a whole, so it doesn’t give insight into how median age at first marriage changed over time. Choice D is incorrect. This choice misreads the graph. The median age of first marriage was consistently higher for men than for women in the United States during the time period depicted.

Urban agriculture is the practice of growing plant- or animal-based products in urban settings such as community gardens and rooftop farms. Esther Sanyé-Mengual, Kathrin Specht, and their team surveyed three groups of people in Bologna, Italy—leaders of urban agriculture projects, stakeholders in urban agriculture (e.g., food researchers and urban farming associations), and the general public—to compare their views about the extent to which urban agriculture contributes to 25 social or ecological services that the team identified. The survey results show that, on average, project leaders rated urban agriculture as contributing less to ______blank
prompt_html: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?

choices_html.A: providing medicinal plants than to improving the local microclimate.
choices_html.B: improving community members’ sense of attachment to the neighborhood than to offering educational opportunities.
choices_html.C: improving the local microclimate than to providing medicinal plants.
choices_html.D: improving the local microclimate than to providing tourist attractions.

rationale_html:
Choice A is the best answer because it most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion about urban agriculture. The graph shows the average survey ratings, on a scale of 0 to 5, from three groups of people—project leaders, stakeholders, and the general public—concerning the contributions of urban agriculture. According to the graph, project leaders gave an average rating of approximately 2 to urban agriculture’s contributions to the provision of medicinal plants, which is lower than the average rating of approximately 3 that project leaders gave to urban agriculture’s contributions to both improving the local microclimate and improving a sense of attachment to the neighborhood. This shows that project leaders rated urban agriculture as contributing less to providing medicinal plants than to improving the local microclimate.

Choice B is incorrect because the graph doesn’t provide data about urban agriculture’s contribution to educational opportunities; therefore, this comparison can’t be made. Choice C is incorrect because it contradicts the data shown in the graph. On average, project leaders gave a rating of approximately 3 to urban agriculture’s contributions to improving the local microclimate, which is higher, not lower, than the average rating of approximately 2 that they gave to its contributions to providing medicinal plants. Choice D is incorrect because the graph doesn’t provide data about urban agriculture’s contribution to providing tourist attractions; therefore, this comparison can’t be made.
